mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from a flat baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 8.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 8.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the predicted negative effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 40%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by accelerating inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the predicted negative effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 40%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month moving averages within the same month indicates a simultaneous expansion in employment and a decline in unemployment, signaling robust labor market health, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average AND UNRATE > 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered months (p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 50%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals elevated household savings relative to spending, which in a high-debt environment often precedes a consumer spending rebound and subsequent earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
regime_hint: post-recession or high household debt regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 40%.
